newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight sees new inquiry in good volume.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight sees new inquiry in good volume.

text.p: Brokers reported a good volume of fresh chartering enquiry, especially for the first half of November from the US Gulf to the Far East.

There seemed to be some confidence that November rates would rise, at least in the grain trades. Panamax routes were again marked up in the BFI which gained 6 points to 1029 but Caper business remained very depressed.

Full details of reported grain fixtures were slow to surface. Glencore were understood to have taken a panamax for meals for mid-Oct from Brazil to China at $22.50 and Continental were linked with Hanjin tonnage US Gulf/S Korea for end Oct.

The Shinwa-relet Top Trader 69,338 dwt was rumoured fixed for US Gulf/Japan, Cho Yang tonnage for NoPac/S Korea and Transfield were said to have covered Vancouver/China, all for Oct loading. Halla have fixed Thalia 64,135 dwt delivery US Gulf Oct 20/28 for a trip to the East at $7,250 daily plus $12,500 bonus, a fair illustration of the flatness of Oct rates when compared with Pan Ocean's fixture last week of Oinoussian Seaman 64,000 dwt in this position at $9,500 daily plus $110,000 bonus.

Halla have also fixed Ateni 63,770 dwt for 3-5 months basis delivery US Gulf end Oct redelivery Atlantic at close to $7,250 daily plus $120,000 bonus, and Ludolf Oldendorff 64,442 dwt delivery NoPac end Oct trip Far East at $7,200 daily plus $120,000 bonus.
Orlando 71,999 dwt was believed to be working closely basis end-Oct in the US Gulf, and Klaveness quoted a fresh order of 55,000 heavy grains US Gulf/Port Klang for Nov 5/15.

A number of new Handy-Size grain orders were seen today in the Atlantic - Cargill with 1.3m cft grain Mississippi/Seaforth for Oct 10/15, for example, Andre 35,000 HSS US Gulf/Constanza Oct 18/25, and Continental 20,000 HSS US Gulf/Morocco for Oct 14/21. There was more activity from S America where up to half a dozen new Handy orders were released including Continental with 225,000 55' Plate/E Med for Oct 20/25 and Andre 22,500 products Plate and Rio Grande to 2 ports S Africa for Oct 18/25. Details of Handy-size fixtures concluded by Toepfer US Gulf/Seaforth, US Gulf/Spanish Med, and Plate/Bangkok and by Continental US Gulf /Morocco have not yet emerged.

This sector made a dull start to the week and rates remain very weak for Capers. Some Panamax tonnage open in positions in the Middle East was reported covered - Delphic Pridey Cobelfret for 60,000 coal Richards Bay/Morocco at $6.75, and Sun P 66,000 dwt on subjects, possibly to Gesuri Lloyd with fertilizers from Aqaba to Indonesia. Atlantic Savior 64,000 dwt was said to be holding firm $7,250 daily plus $125,000 bonus for a trip with fertilizers from NoPac to the Far East but holding out for more.

Handy-Sizes. The promise of the market on the Continent for owners of smaller Handies has evaporated to some extent. An over-age 22,000 dwt vessel obtained only $6,000 daily with spot delivery for a trip to W Coast S America, but a similar vessel was fixed at $8,250 daily plus $20,000 bonus for a trip from the Continent to the Far East. Beta 40,010 dwt was rumoured to have gone for scrap from the Continent to Turkey at a higher rate than last fixed.

The S African market is also weak for small Handies - IVS, for example, picked up a 26,000 dwt bulker for a trip to the Continent at $3,750 daily option Med at $4,000. But the Handymaxes are not so cheap and MOSK were believed to have fixed Santarita 41,000 dwt Richards Bay/Japan at $7,500 daily plus $100,000 bonus. In the Far East Canpotex booked Pisces Planter 35,000 dwt delivery NoPac for a trip with Potash to the Far East at an unchanged $6,500 daily plus $100,000 bonus.
